correctness.rationale: An exact pathwise renewal law yields probability weight (h/2)^K for a prescribed final successful route. Parity forces extra hops in pairs; for fixed interval, nonshortest paths have O(h²) conditional mass. The tilted Mittag-Leffler law has a signed Gamma expansion absolutely convergent in total variation, enabling a norm-level m-fold product and Dirichlet pushforward. Beta-Gamma moments prove zero mean and strict nonconstancy of the signed correction. For beta=1, normalized exponential waits give exactly uniform Dirichlet shares and brute path counting gives c/4 h². The standalone executable performed 2804 deterministic tests; the proof does not infer infinity from finite enumeration.

value.rationale: The residence-time fraction vector is a natural, time-unit invariant path-resolved observable for subdiffusive CTRWs. Its finite-reset approximation error is now known to leading order with a positive computable Dirichlet expectation, and the exponential-clock limit loses this first-order term exactly, changing the error exponent. This resolves an experimentally interpretable contrast not determined by endpoint splitting or elapsed-time moments and applies for all fixed interval geometries with a shortest path of length at least two.
